title: Exceptions and logging

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
Logging records events in a running service with levels and handlers; `print` does not provide that control.
Logging records events in a running service with levels and handlers;
print
does not provide that control.
CORE EXPLANATION
Catch expected failures by their specific exception type; broad except blocks can hide programming bugs. logging records time and severity; show users a safe, clear message.

LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`import logging` — Imports functionality from a module; without it, the name is unavailable and may raise NameError.
`logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
`try:` — Marks operations that may fail; without a handler, an expected error can stop the caller.
`amount = int('7')` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`except ValueError:` — This line continues the calculation or control flow; omitting it removes that step and may change later results.
`logging.exception('Invalid amount')` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Never write passwords, tokens, or personal data to logs.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: Broad except Exception and especially bare except should not silently swallow failures.
